content.title: How the debut of Kim Mulkey as LSU women's basketball coach was a smashing success
content.text: Updated Nov. 9, 2021, 3:11 p.m. CTKim Mulkey was welcomed back to her home state – after a long stay away – with much fanfare in late April.Six-plus months after leaving a job she held for more than two decades, the Tickfaw native finally got to work her first game as LSU women’s basketball coach.Mulkey’s debut was a smashing success, an 82-40 win over Nicholls on Tuesday in front of an announced crowd of 5,357 at the Maravich Assembly Center that included thousands of noise-making students making field trips from greater Baton Rouge area schools and several of Mulkey’s own friends and family members.“We had a lot of North Louisiana, Louisiana Tech, people that came, and my family is here,” said Mulkey, who was associate head coach at Louisiana Tech for four seasons from 1996-2000 after spending 11 seasons as an assistant. “It’s wonderful. It’s wonderful that they can share in it with me.“The thing about it is, they’re expensive. I had to feed them all weekend. They’ve been here since Friday. … I’m kidding. They like to eat like I do. I’ve got to get this weight off me. I knew when I came down here that I was gonna gain because I’m eating things I haven’t had in 40 years. Gosh, it’s wonderful.”Mulkey surely can afford the food bill.LSU used an eight-year, $23.75 million contract to lure her was away from Baylor, where she spent 21 seasons and won national championships in 2005, 2012 and 2019.She replaced Nikki Fargas, who resigned after going 176-128 in 10 seasons at LSU. Fargas is now president of WNBA’s Las Vegas Aces.Coincidentally, All-SEC guard Khayla Pointer, the niece of Fargas, led the Tigers Tuesday with 16 points, 13 assists and 11 rebounds – the fourth triple-double in program history.“We’re out there, we’re playing such a fast tempo, and Coach instills confidence in each and every one of us,” Pointer said. “You know, we’re out there and we’re playing confident. We let it fly. … It’s fun out there. You can see we’re out there having fun.”LSU led 39-10 at halftime after shooting 17-of-34 from the field while limiting Nicholls to 4-of-22 shooting. The Tigers ended the half on a 17-0 run.LSU, which faces Florida Gulf Coast on Sunday (12:30 p.m., SEC Network+) before playing its first road game Nov. 18 at UL, finished 34-of-64 (53.1%) from the field.Mulkey, whose team was picked to finish eighth in the SEC by the conference’s head coaches, loved the defensive effort.“We have to defend, and we have to defend the entire court the entire game, no matter what the score is,” she said.“We have to get in that mode. We know what we face this year, and how talented the teams are, particularly in the SEC, so just defend, quit looking at the clock, and we know we’ve to do that to have a chance to beat some people that we are not even supposed to beat.”
